title: Powerhouse packages are published to NPM and installed into host apps via ph install
content:
Powerhouse packages follow a standard publishing workflow:

1. **Package naming**: Scoped convention `@your-org-ph/your-package-name` (the `-ph` suffix identifies Powerhouse ecosystem packages)
2. **powerhouse.manifest.json**: Declares package contents - document models (with document type IDs) and editors (linked to document types). Before the first publish, set its `name`, `description`, and `publisher`, and make `package.json`'s `name` match
3. **Build**: `pnpm build` or `npm run build` compiles to dist/
4. **Publish**: `npm login` then `npm publish` (with `"publishConfig": { "access": "public" }` for scoped packages), or `ph publish --registry=<url>`
5. **Install**: `ph install @your-org-ph/your-package-name` makes document models and editors available in any Powerhouse environment

`ph install` defaults to the **Powerhouse registry**: it only registers the package in `powerhouse.config.json` with provider `"registry"`, and Connect loads it from the registry CDN at runtime -- it does NOT install into `node_modules` by default. Use `--local` to also install into `node_modules` (provider `"local"`) so `ph connect build` bundles it and the preview works without the registry being reachable. Registry URL resolution order: `--registry` flag > `PH_REGISTRY_URL` env > `powerhouse.config.json` > default.

The scaffolded `package.json` `files` array contains only `["/dist"]` -- the compiled build output is what ships, not the source `document-models` / `editors` folders.

Semantic versioning is used for package versions. The AGPL-3.0-only license is common in the ecosystem.

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: Packages use scoped NPM names (@org-ph/name), include powerhouse.manifest.json, and are installed with `ph install @org/package`.
